entries.original: Standalone `omo update` now installs the release instead of printing a curl command (#13084). It downloads the matching platform asset from get.omo.dev with GitHub fallback, verifies published SHA256SUMS and the existing macOS signature, stages beside the installed executable, and keeps a rollback copy until the installed `--version` succeeds. Failures report a typed error; an unwritable directory is refused without partial files. Windows rollback files still held by a running process are cleaned on a later launch. `--dry-run` and `--print` remain print-only. ([#13087](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13087))

entries.original: `omo login --new-device` is gone. The OmO service keeps one device per computer, so registering another device over an unreadable stored sign-in either failed after approval or left two live devices. When the stored sign-in cannot be read, `omo login` gives one recovery: remove this computer's device on the Devices page if it is still listed, then run `omo account forget` (which also has the device service forget the device), then sign in again. When the device service holds the device, it also names that device and says these steps sign out the device service, and the OmO desktop app if it is installed, on this computer. ([#13276](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13276)) ([#13328](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13328))

entries.original: Computer use v3: the engine's result and error contract lands in `omo-computer-core`: `Disposition` with exactly the seven valid `(delivery, retry)` pairs, `ActionReport` with receipts decided by verb (a value verb is `confirmed` only on a read-back equal to what it requested, a pointer or key verb only on an OS-level consumption receipt), wire validation that refuses an overclaiming report, and the one `COMPUTER_*` table keyed by `(engineCode, data.reason)`, total over the closed engine codes and every reason the design emits, checked against a cited inventory of the design. Backend refusals and exec replies now resolve through it. Nothing user-visible changes yet; the existing desktop engine is untouched. entries.original: Desktop memory sync no longer risks running out of memory on an oversized reply from the sync service. zod moves to 4.6.7 (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5: validating a huge array collected one issue per bad element), and every array the sync channel reads is now capped at 100,000 items, so an oversized reply is rejected up front. This release pins senpi 2026.11.13. The only zod below 4.6.6 that still ships is the copy the Claude agent SDK embeds in its prebuilt code, which is used only to parse the local Claude Code subprocess output. ([#13151](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13151)) ([#13141](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13141))
